items.readable_text:
Content:
A continuous random variable [MATH: X] follows a continuous uniform distribution on the interval [MATH: [a,b]] if all values of [MATH: X] are equally likely on [MATH: [a,b].]

Content:
Intuitively, the familiar statement "choose a random number between [MATH: a] and [MATH: b]" can be translated as "observe a value from the continuous uniform distribution on [MATH: [a,b].]"

Content:
The probability density function for the continuous uniform distribution on an interval [MATH: [a,b]] takes the following form:

Content:
[MATH: {(1)/(b − a),|a ≤ x ≤ b,; 0,|otherwise]

Content:
This corresponds to the following graph:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/9c3cae382fec34384828202a115a8cd3]

Content:
Notice that the probability density of the continuous uniform distribution on [MATH: [a,b]] is just [MATH: 1] divided by the length of the interval. This ensures that our probability density function has the same value everywhere in the interval and integrates to [MATH: 1{:}]

Content:
[MATH: ∫_{a}^{b}(1)/(b − a)dx|= (x)/(b − a)|_{a}^{b}; = (b − a)/(b − a); = 1✓]

Content:
When a random variable [MATH: X] follows a continuous uniform distribution on the interval [MATH: [a,b],] we often write

Content:
[MATH: X\sim U[a,b]]

Content:
and say that "[MATH: X] is uniformly distributed on the interval [MATH: [a,b].]"

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable [MATH: X] on an interval [MATH: [a,b]] is given by

[MATH: {(1)/(b − a),|a ≤ x ≤ b,; 0,|otherwise.]

Our random variable [MATH: X] is uniformly distributed on the interval [MATH: \left[0, 10\right],] so it has the following probability density function:

[MATH: {(1)/(10),|0 ≤ x ≤ 10,; 0,|otherwise.]

So, we have

[MATH: P(X ≤ 7)|= P(0 ≤ X ≤ 7); = ∫_{0}^{7}f(x)dx; = ∫_{0}^{7}(1)/(10)dx; = (7 − 0)/(10); = (7)/(10).]

Item 2 — Example: Computing a "Less Than" Probability for a Uniformly Distributed Continuous Random Variable

Example Prompt:
Given that the continuous random variable [MATH: X] is uniformly distributed on the interval [MATH: \left[0, 10\right],] compute [MATH: P\left(X \leq 7\right).]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable [MATH: X] on an interval [MATH: [a,b]] is given by

[MATH: {(1)/(b − a),|a ≤ x ≤ b,; 0,|otherwise.]

Our random variable [MATH: X] is uniformly distributed on the interval [MATH: \left[0, 10\right],] so it has the following probability density function:

[MATH: {(1)/(10),|0 ≤ x ≤ 10,; 0,|otherwise.]

So, we have

[MATH: P(X ≤ 7)|= P(0 ≤ X ≤ 7); = ∫_{0}^{7}f(x)dx; = ∫_{0}^{7}(1)/(10)dx; = (7 − 0)/(10); = (7)/(10).]
